ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A circuit containing an ideal transformer is shown in the figure. In the figure, the resistance values of resistors R1, R2, and R3 are respectively 3Ω, 1Ω, and 4Ω; it is an ideal AC ammeter; U is a sinusoidal AC voltage source, and the effective value of the output voltage is constant. When switch S is open, the reading of the ammeter is I; when S is closed, the reading of the ammeter is 4I. The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of this transformer is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A circuit containing an ideal transformer is shown in the figure. In the figure, the resistance values of resistors R1, R2, and R3 are respectively 3Ω, 1Ω, and 4Ω. U is a sinusoidal AC voltage source, and the effective value of the output voltage is constant. When switch S is open, the reading of the ammeter is I; when S is closed, the reading of the ammeter is 4I. What is the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of this transformer?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is a sinusoidal AC power supply U. The ammeter A, fixed-value resistor R1, and the primary coil of the ideal transformer are connected in series; the right side is the secondary coil of the transformer, and the secondary-side load is composed of R2 and R3 connected in series up and down. Switch S is connected between the midpoint of R2 and R3 and the lower-end node; therefore, when S is closed, R3 will be short-circuited, and when S is open, R2 and R3 are connected in series across the two ends of the secondary coil. Reasoning: It is known that R1=3Ω, R2=1Ω, R3=4Ω. When S is open, the secondary-side load is R2+R3=1+4=5Ω; when S is closed, R3 is short-circuited, and the secondary-side load is R2=1Ω. Let the turns ratio of the transformer primary and secondary coils be k=N1/N2. In an ideal transformer, a secondary-side resistance R is converted to the primary side as k^2R. Thus when S is open, the total resistance on the primary side is 3+5k^2, and the ammeter reading is I=U/(3+5k^2); when S is closed, the total resistance on the primary side is 3+k^2, and the ammeter reading is U/(3+k^2). The problem states that the reading after closing is 4I, so U/(3+k^2)=4U/(3+5k^2). Cancel U and cross-multiply: 3+5k^2=4(3+k^2)=12+4k^2, obtaining k^2=9, and taking the positive value gives k=3.
